key_insight: Intra-patient 3D multimodal registration remains unsolved: the best method depends on anatomy, modality, and whether overlap or global structural correspondence is prioritized.
engineering_relevance: For clinical imaging pipelines, method selection should be benchmarked on the target anatomy with multiple metrics, because high Dice does not guarantee accurate multimodal alignment.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based deformable registration methods.
Compared performance across three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical cases.
Evaluated with complementary metrics: DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC.
evidence_signal: Across three datasets, learning-based methods performed best on large synthetic benchmarks, while gains were limited in real pelvic registration and geometric metrics often disagreed with MIND-SSC.
watch_item: High overlap on segmented regions can mask poor global correspondence outside labels, so anatomy-guided models should be checked for deformation quality beyond ROI metrics.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
